name: std::assignable_from
intro: The concept assignable_from<LHS, RHS> specifies that an expression of the type and value category specified by RHS can be assigned to an lvalue expression whose type is specified by LHS.

sections.title: Semantic requirements
Equality preservation
sections.text: Expressions declared in requires expressions of the standard library concepts are required to be equality-preserving (except where stated otherwise).

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: Assignment need not be a total function. In particular, if assigning to some object x can cause some other object y to be modified, then x = y is likely not in the domain of =. This typically happens if the right operand is owned directly or indirectly by the left operand (e.g., with smart pointers to nodes in a node-based data structure, or with something like std::vector<std::any>).
